summary:
TakeOFF is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring system designed to support crew members during long-duration space missions. It consists of three integrated components: a Crew Health Client for recording and locally storing health observations, a FastAPI backend for secure data management and synchronization, and a Ground Health Console for medical officers to monitor crew health remotely.

TakeOFF allows astronauts to record health indicators, review health observations and trends, and communicate with ground medical teams. Its store-and-forward synchronization architecture helps preserve health records during communication delays or blackouts, while enabling data transfer when connectivity returns. Medical officers can review observations, send follow-up instructions, and track crew acknowledgements.

The system also incorporates NASA's OSD-575 research dataset as a separate retrospective reference, without confusing research records with live telemetry. TakeOFF aims to make health monitoring more accessible, resilient and actionable, helping astronauts and medical teams identify concerns and respond during missions far from Earth.
details:
TakeOFF is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring and decision-support system designed for long-duration space missions. It consists of three integrated components:

1. Crew Health Client: A desktop application where astronauts can record health measurements, complete daily check-ins, review health history, monitor trends and compare supported measurements against personal baselines. It stores records locally using SQLite, allowing health-data collection and local analysis to continue during communication interruptions.

2. FastAPI Backend: Handles authentication, data storage, synchronization and communication between astronauts and ground medical teams.

3. Ground Health Console: A web dashboard that enables medical officers to review synchronized astronaut health observations, examine assessments, monitor data freshness and communication status, and send messages or follow-up instructions to the crew.

TakeOFF uses a simulated communication adapter with LIVE, DELAYED and BLACKOUT states. During interruptions, observations remain stored locally and queued for synchronization when connectivity becomes available.

Its key benefit is that astronauts can continue monitoring and recording their health without depending on continuous communication with Earth. Personal-baseline comparisons and historical trends help make measurements more understandable, while two-way communication supports medical oversight.

The project uses React, TypeScript and Tauri for the desktop application; Python and FastAPI for the backend; SQLite for local storage; and PostgreSQL for the ground-side database architecture. NASA's OSD-575 dataset is also integrated as a separate retrospective research resource for exploring spaceflight-related biomarker changes.

TakeOFF's creative approach lies in combining offline-first health monitoring, local analysis, resilient synchronization and ground medical collaboration into one system. The design considers communication delays, limited access to medical assistance, individual health variations, data provenance, privacy and the need to distinguish missing or unreliable measurements from genuine health concerns.

Our intended impact is to help astronauts better understand and monitor their health while enabling ground medical teams to remain informed and provide follow-up support, even when communication with Earth is interrupted.
